catalyst_text: Reported positive 12 month OLE results in PAH
detailed_catalyst_text: The company reported positive 12‑month results from an ongoing open‑label extension study in pulmonary arterial hypertension, showing sustained improvements in 6MWD, NT‑proBNP, WHO Functional Class, and REVEAL Lite 2.0, with no new safety signals up to 1,280 µg once daily. Additionally, a Phase 3 trial (PALM‑PAH) has been recently initiated in this indication. These data and the advancement to Phase 3 underscore the program’s progression and potential clinical impact.
catalyst_text_evidence: BRIDGEWATER, N.J., 2026-07-16 /PRNewswire/ -- Insmed Incorporated (NASDAQ:INSM)... today announced positive 12-Month data from the ongoing open-label extension (OLE) study evaluating treprostinil palmitil inhalation powder (TPIP), administered once daily in patients with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH, World Health Organization Group 1). Results for secondary efficacy endpoints demonstrated sustained improvement with TPIP in six-minute walk distance (6MWD), N-terminal fragment pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) concentration, and World Health Organization (WHO) Functional Class, as well as a clinically meaningful improvement in REVEAL Lite 2.0 score at Month 12. Results for the primary endpoint of safety & tolerability showed that once-daily TPIP therapy was generally well tolerated with no newly identified safety signals at doses up to 1,280 µg through Month 12. The 12-Month OLE findings support the continued clinical development of TPIP and the recent initiation of PALM-PAH, a Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluating once-daily TPIP in patients with PAH over 24 weeks.

catalyst_text: Reported negative topline Phase 2b results in HS
detailed_catalyst_text: Topline results from the randomized, double-blind Phase 2b CEDAR study in adults with moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa showed the trial did not meet primary or secondary efficacy endpoints at 10 mg or 40 mg. Safety was consistent with prior experience, with no new safety signals observed, including at the highest dose tested. These negative findings indicate a lack of clinical efficacy for this indication.
catalyst_text_evidence: “today announced that the Phase 2b CEDAR study, which evaluated brensocatib in adult patients with moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa (HS), did not meet its primary or secondary efficacy endpoints in either the 10 mg or 40 mg treatment arms.” “Brensocatib was well tolerated, with no new safety signals identified, including in the 40 mg arm, which is the highest dose Insmed has studied to date.” “CEDAR was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, Phase 2b study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of brensocatib in adults with moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa.”

catalyst_text: Announced positive topline Phase 3 results meeting endpoints
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive topline results from the randomized, double-blind Phase 3b ENCORE trial in MAC lung disease showed statistically significant improvements in respiratory symptom score and culture conversion versus comparator. The study was completed and intended to fulfill an FDA post‑marketing requirement, strengthening the clinical foundation for this therapy in this population.
catalyst_text_evidence: The Study Met Primary and All Multiplicity-Controlled Secondary Culture Conversion Endpoints, Demonstrating Statistically Significant and Clinically Meaningful Improvements in Respiratory Symptom Score and Culture Conversion Rates BRIDGEWATER, N.J., 2026-03-23 /PRNewswire/ -- Insmed Incorporated (NASDAQ:INSM), a people-first global biopharmaceutical company striving to deliver first- and best-in-class therapies to transform the lives of patients facing serious diseases, today announced positive topline results from the Phase 3b ENCORE study. With these results, Insmed has completed the study intended to fulfill the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) post-marketing requirement, further strengthening the clinical foundation supporting ARIKAYCE.
